title: 1975-11-05_SECTION_013_14.txt
concise_summary: In this entry PKD consolidates his identification of the feminine figure from his 2-3-74 visions as St. Sophia/Nous, the Logos and steersperson of the universe, arguing she is simultaneously the Pantocrator, the Cosmic Christ, and the teleological Omega of Teilhard de Chardin. He then executes an extended typological reading of his 1970 novel 'Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said' (TEARS), arguing the novel prophetically depicted the slave-state conditions of Nixon's America, the divine intervention of 1974, and the salvific mechanism of Christian agape — making TEARS a steganographic apocalyptic text in which the Logos speaks itself into history. The entry integrates Platonic cosmology (Timaeus), Gnostic concepts (dokos, Nous), and New Testament eschatology (Parousia, the Day of Judgment) into a unified framework in which his own fiction functions as divinely sanctioned prophecy.
key_claims: The female figure from the 3-74 visions is St. Sophia/Nous, the sole steersperson of the universe, identical with the Logos, the Pantocrator, and the Cosmic Christ.
Nous conceals its activity behind dokos (appearance/illusion) as a strategic weapon against its Adversary, making invisibility essential to the cosmic game.

PKD's novel TEARS (Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said, written 1970) prophetically depicted the Nixon slave-state, the divine intervention of 1974, and the salvific role of Christian love — it is an apocalyptic text encoding the Parousia.
The Parousia — the Second Coming of Christ — actually occurred in 1974 in the form of St. Sophia's intervention that toppled Nixon, fulfilling the Book of Daniel and Revelation.
Nixon was functionally or literally diabolic — 'Satan at the heart of the citadel' — whose removal by divine judgment enabled the entry of agape into the world.
The 3-74 visions were granted to PKD specifically because he had written TEARS, making the conferral an act of justice rather than mere mercy: the prophet was shown what his prophecy had depicted.
recurring_concepts: Nous (divine mind, cosmic intelligence, identified with St. Sophia and the Logos)
Dokos (illusory veil concealing Nous's activity from the Adversary)
St. Sophia (feminine divine wisdom, ultimate steersperson and Pantocrator of the universe)
Logos (the active divine Word, identified with St. Sophia and the salvific principle)
Parousia (Second Coming, which PKD argues occurred in 1974)
Ananke (blind efficient cause, the brute force that Sophia perpetually outmaneuvers)
Steganographia (hidden writing within TEARS that encodes apocalyptic truth)
The Adversary (cosmic antagonist opposing Nous, identified with or embodied in the Roman Empire and Nixon)
Agape (Pauline love as the salvific force introduced into the world by divine intervention)
Omega / teleological principle (Teilhard de Chardin's concept applied to St. Sophia as the final goal of the universe)
people_entities: St. Sophia — Gnostic/Christian divine feminine wisdom figure; PKD's primary name for the entity revealed in his 2-3-74 visions
Teilhard de Chardin — Jesuit theologian and paleontologist; PKD cites his concept of Omega as the teleological endpoint of the universe
Plato — Greek philosopher; PKD invokes the Timaeus for its cosmological account of the Demiurge/Nous
Richard Nixon — 37th U.S. president; PKD identifies him as functionally diabolic, 'Satan at the heart of the citadel,' whose removal constituted divine judgment
Senator Lowell Weicker — U.S. Senator who spoke against Nixon; PKD cites his statement about loving enemies as the moment Christian agape entered the political world
General Sherman — U.S. Civil War general; PKD briefly invokes him as an instance of Roman-style tyranny breaking through in American history
Hitler — compared to Nixon as another instance of genuinely diabolic evil at the center of political power
Joel — unnamed friend or acquaintance who argued the U.S. is the pivot point of world freedom and declared the Xerox letter probably a U.S. forgery
Kathy — person appearing in a Canada dream in which she and others removed their masks; appears to be a real acquaintance of PKD
Buckman — fictional character in TEARS (Felix Buckman); his internal change toward loving his enemies is PKD's key example of agape entering the slave state
Taverner — fictional character in TEARS (Jason Taverner); his vindication represents the turn from oppression to justice
The wise old king — figure from TEARS who breaches through and raises the siege; PKD reads him as the Ancient of Days / Christ the King
texts_works: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said (TEARS) — PKD's 1970 novel; central to this entry as apocalyptic prophecy of 1974 events
The Bible — cited as correct about the Logos/Sophia
Plato, Timaeus — cited for its account of Nous and the construction of the cosmos
Acts of the Apostles — referenced in relation to material incorporated in TEARS
Book of Daniel — cited regarding the Ancient of Days and End Times judgment
Book of Revelation — cited regarding calamitous aspects of the End Times
Sermon on the Mount — cited for 'Love your enemies' as the highest expression of agape
autobiographical: PKD describes his 2-3-74 visions as having been 'dreamt for him' — not self-generated but imposed by an external divine agency
He records seeing in the visions a smiling female figure (St. Sophia) outmaneuvering a 'baleful force' with superior wisdom, and states 'I loved her smile'
He describes receiving the visions as a great privilege and continually asking why he was chosen
He recalls a dream set in Canada in which a woman named Kathy and others removed their masks — connected to a larger pattern of hidden identity
He mentions a 'pale white light' experienced in August (of 1974) as a distinct mystical event distinct from the narrative visions
He refers to the 'Xerox letter' — apparently a mysterious letter PKD received or sent, which his friend Joel speculated was a U.S. government forgery — as related to the intervention narrative
He describes 'elaborate changes made in me, end-time changes' that preceded the August pale white light experience
He recalls the popular tune played over a Catholic radio station as a possible signal whose significance he cannot quite determine
theological_motifs: Parousia — the Second Coming of Christ, which PKD argues occurred in 1974 in the form of Sophia's intervention
Pantocrator — Ruler of All; PKD applies this title to St. Sophia on the grounds that she judged, judged downward, and executed her own judgment
Cosmic Christ — title PKD applies to Sophia, linking her salvific power to Christ
Day of Judgment / End Times — PKD argues the Judgment depicted in Daniel and Revelation was fulfilled in 1974
Agape (Pauline love) — the salvific force introduced into history by divine intervention; its introduction is what causes the slave-state apparatus to wither
Anamnesis — sudden remembering of one's true identity (referenced in evidence_excerpts from adjacent sections); implied in PKD's recognition of himself as an early Christian
Continuous creation — Nous joins weak or bad elements to make good ones, a process PKD observed in his visions
Teleology / Omega point — Sophia as the final cause and goal of the universe, aligned with Teilhard's Omega
Steganographia — hidden divine writing within the text of TEARS, particularly the inserted dream sequence
Salvation — PKD identifies the visions themselves as part of the salvific process: Sophia restoring lost faculties or conferring miraculous sight
literary_self_ref: PKD argues TEARS (Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said) is an apocalyptic text that prophetically depicted the Nixon slave state, the divine intervention of 1974, and the salvific role of agape — written before these events occurred
He identifies the 'wise old king' who breaches through in TEARS with the Ancient of Days / Christ the King who intervened in actual history in 1974
He reads Buckman's internal transformation toward loving his enemies as the fictional analog of the introduction of agape into the real world after Nixon's fall

He argues the dream sequence he inserted into TEARS (originally dreamed without any connection to its social themes) was itself an act of St. Sophia joining two disparate elements — the novelist's unconscious and the prophetic narrative
He speculates that some readers of TEARS decoded its steganographic message, with two groups receiving it — one inside and one outside the tyranny
He states that TEARS is most of all why he was granted the 3-74 visions: 'It is because of TEARS most of all that I was shown what I was shown'
symbols_images: The smiling female figure — St. Sophia seen in the visions, always smiling as she outmaneuvers the baleful force
The veil (dokos) — the illusion that conceals Nous's activity from the Adversary
The world as raw material / stockpile — earth as the building material Nous uses to construct a new heaven and earth
We are within a construct which she is building; it is a kind of body — the cosmos as Sophia's body under construction
The wise old king breaching through the wall — the figure in TEARS who raises the siege, read as the Ancient of Days
Five police marshals against the wise old king — the opposition between state power and divine authority in TEARS
The all-night gas station with the black man — the scene in TEARS where agape is enacted; PKD's key image of love entering the slave world
The pale white light — the August 1974 mystical experience PKD treats as distinct from and supplementary to the visions
Masks being removed — the Canada dream in which Kathy and others revealed their true faces
The Xerox letter — a material artifact in PKD's life connected to the intervention narrative, possibly a forgery
The Catholic radio station and popular tune — ambiguous signal possibly connected to the hidden communications of the cosmic game
Invisible nucleus of evil replaced by invisible nucleus of good — the hidden structural transformation PKD believes occurred in 1974
tensions: PKD equates St. Sophia with the Logos, the Pantocrator, and the Cosmic Christ but also calls her feminine and by a Gnostic name (Sophia) — this produces an unresolved tension between Gnostic cosmology, where Sophia is subordinate or fallen, and PKD's elevation of her to supreme cosmic ruler

He claims the visions were 'dreamt for me' and that he was a passive recipient, yet also argues the visions were granted specifically because he had actively written TEARS — implying he earned or merited the vision, which conflicts with pure grace
PKD states he would 'not want to know' whether readers decoded TEARS's message but then immediately speculates that 'yes, two groups' did receive it — a self-correction he does not fully resolve

He identifies Sophia with the Pantocrator (who judges downward and executes judgment) but also with agape and a 'smiling' figure who defeats evil lovingly — the combination of wrathful judge and loving wisdom-figure is theologically unresolved

He equates the Parousia definitively with 1974 but then notes Daniel and Revelation 'may have overstressed the calamitous aspects for cautionary purposes' — suggesting uncertainty about how literally to read apocalyptic scripture alongside his own literalistic reading of current events
The text breaks off mid-sentence ('that is probably the') leaving the final claim incomplete — creating an unresolved textual gap
evidence_quotes: I saw Nous obscuring its plays with dokos, so the Adversary could not fathom its moves; I saw continuous creation as Nous joined two weak, imperfect or bad sections to become a good one; the veil (dokos) is necessary because of the Game & Nous' adversary.
There is only one steersperson for this universe; my experience is by St. Sophia and about St. Sophia.
What I saw was the, not just a. We are within a construct which she is building; it is a kind of body.
It is because of TEARS most of all that I was shown what I was shown; mark what I have said here, and recall, too, the material from Acts in TEARS, and the topic of Pauline agape or love.
I think now that there is a certain justice in conferring the 3-74 experience/visions on the author of TEARS; justice and appropriateness more than mercy or kindness.
uncertainty_flags: PKD refers to 'the Xerox letter' and 'two letters' as if these are known referents, but the identity and content of these letters is unclear and Joel's claim that they were likely a U.S. government forgery is unverified
The 'Canada dream' with Kathy and the mask-removal is mentioned as if previously discussed but is not explained in this segment — the identity of 'Kathy' and the dream's narrative context are unclear
PKD mentions 'a popular tune played over the Catholic radio' as possibly a signal, but provides no further detail — the tune, the station, and the signaling relationship are entirely unspecified

The claim that TEARS was 'written in 1970' is PKD's own dating; the novel was published in 1974, so there may be a discrepancy between composition date and publication date that affects the prophetic claim
The text ends mid-sentence ('that is probably the') suggesting this is a fragment and the full argument about 'end-time changes' made in PKD is not preserved in this segment

PKD attributes the 'Love your enemies' speech to Senator Weicker but the specific speech or statement is not identified — a scholar should verify whether Weicker used this formulation in a public context around 1974
reading_excerpt: There is only one steersperson for this universe; my experience is by St. Sophia and about St. Sophia.
raw_text: as you imagine, or anyhow as Someone imagines. If I wasn't already right about physical reality this couldn't have happened; it is a kind of dream, but I was not the dreamer. It was dremt for me. Of course I could go the route which religious mystics usually go and say, "I was taken out of mundane space & time and transported back to ancient Rome" or "...shown ancient Rome, and then I later was shown a vision of the Promised Land," without going into the mechanics of it. This, then, presumes that the two visions were a form of language, to com¬ municate something to me. Most of all: I saw Nous obscuring its plays with dokos, so the Adversary could not fathom its moves; I saw continuous creation as Nous joined two weak, imperfect or bad sections to become a good one; the veil (dokos) is necessary because of the Game & Nous' ad¬ versary .. .who seems to be either in this world or actually this world, which is the stockpile for Nous' building. Nous is invisibly building a new heavens and earth, using this earth for raw material, despite the adversary's efforts. Concealment of this is necessary, even from us, who seem portions of this world. (We're on the wrong side?) In summation: one of the greatest (and most vital) weapons the spirit has is her invisibility, which extends to the pattern of her plays. Thus I deduce that it was a great privilege that she gave me a glimpse of herself & her activity; also I deduce that I am not with the Adversary, or she wouldn't have let me see what I saw. One must be taken over by the spirit to see her & her activity, evi¬ dently. In which case I might say that the ultimate secret of the universe, the major undisclosed thing, is the spirit & her activity. She works within the world, unseen. This is the ultimate entity, as far as we and our world are concerned. What is her name? I guess St. Sophia, or Nous. I saw more than I realized; I saw all. This is the logos, the ultimate active agency in our universe; our salvation depends on her & her alone. I loved her smile. Teilhard was right: she is also the ultimate goal, Omega, of the universe: the teleological principle and agent and force and outcome. 5- If I view her as the ultimate good agency of our universe, then surely I have been grated the greatest vision possible. I will always wonder why. Anyhow I cherish it. Wow. To see her defeat the baleful force over & over again, and always smiling, always wiser than that huge blind drive of efficient cause (ananke). The Bible is right (about her, the logos) but also Plato is right in Timaeus. What I saw was the, not just a. We are within a construct which she is building; it is a kind of body. I am more & more convinced that the agency (or entity) which brought me the 3-74 experience (visions) is the agency (or entity) revealed in the visions, since the more I am sure that the female figure is the guide of the universe and hence St. Sophia the more see seems the sole agency or entity capable of producing such visions. There is only one steersperson for this universe; my experience is by St. Sophia and about St. Sophia. This adds to everything else she was shown capable of in the visions themselves the ability to (whichever it is) restore the lost faculties or to confer miraculous sight; in either case this is an aspect of the salvific process, and identifies her again as the Cosmic Christ. The totality of atributes which she possesses certainly makes her the Pantocrator; for instance, she was not only witnessing the acts of the conspirators but she was judging and punishing those acts; who is this if not the Pantocrator? Then I say, I have been granted the miracle of beeing allowed to see the Pantocrator judging. What is this if not the Parousia? By definition of the Greek word: His Second Coming. In history, the invisible nucleus of evil has been replaced by the invisible nucleus of good; the plans of evil did not come to fruition but were removed with it (the plans were to recreate the ancient slave society, with the plutocracy living off it, as in Roman times). (I.e the reestablish the worst aspects of the Roman Empire, inside and out.) But, as in TEARS, which depicted all this, the turning point came when the wise old king burst through the breach with his armed hosts; amelioration began, justice set in, and the slave state withered away in the end. What happened to us (the bad: the slave state, then the heavenly intervention) is depicted in TEARS; what has been invislbe here is visible there. Thus TEARS, which was written and published before the intervention, is a very important book when viewed this way (i.e. as apocalyptic, showing what was going to happen — and it did). It is because of TEARS most of all that I was shown what I was shown; mark what I have said here, and recall, too, the material from Acts in TEARS, and the topic of Pauline agape or love. TEARS, then, is a vision of two things hidden by the dokos: a vision of the evil & its plans; a vision of the good & its intervention, and the nature of both set forth (the five police marshals against the wise old king). It is the police against God, with God turning the tide (i.e. the internal change in Buckman which causes him to do something absolutely not in character). "Love your enemies," epitimizes what he does: from the Sermon on the Mount, the highest form of love, and salvific. The Great Change begins in Buckman, and spreads out from there, with the vindication of Taverner. -6- It is interesting how the insertion of my actual dream into TEARS exemplifies the joining of two items by St. Sophia, since in my own life the dream when I dreamed it had nothing to do with my society or the extension-into-visibility of it which I had already laid out in the novel. But juxtiposed, they made their historic (apocalyptic) point. I think now that there is a certain justice in conferring the 3-74 experience/visions on the author of TEARS; justice and appropriateness more than mercy or kindness. TEARS says: "This bad situation exists or will soon exist or anyhow is planned, and it will end — in the following way," and it discloses the way (the Intervention). The wise old king breaches through & raises the siege. We were prisoners in a great prison, until he broke through to redeem us. The stegenographia in TEARS is not limited to the dream section but is throughout, with the dream section the heavenly insertion, within the evil body (our world, the depictment of it). It is of another color — the logos speaking itself. It was to all this understanding that the dream in Canada referred, in which Kathy & the others took off their masks. Again I wonder, Did anyone exist who received TEARS and decoded the message? but knowledge of that is mercifully denied me. (I really would not want to know; it is too heavy. But I think yes, two groups, one inside the evil tyranny, the other outside.) Maybe it was the popular tune played over the Catholic radio, signal that... I wonder. Well, that is beyond my purview. The idea "Prisons are a source of wealth" has been defeated. The return to Roman ways occured in the U.S., in the Civil War, espoused by General Sherman; the Germans learned from him. The antique tyranny broke through once more! The empire on the north (King of the North), the slavery on the south (King of the South). Now, let us start with TEARS as the paradigm print-out, of our society. What, then, does TEARS tell us as to the saving force? What is it? Why, clearly it is God; clearly Christ the King has come; again, by this route, we come to believe that the Parousia took place, for TEARS said it did. People do not notice the event in actuality, nor understand it when they read TEARS, mainly because they are not looking for it and would not know it —did not— were it to come; in TEARS there can be no doubt — the Ancient of Days is clearly depicted. Also (il) He judged; (2) He judged against or downward; (3) He executed his own judgment. In this world the 3-eyed lady (1) Judged; (2) judged downward; (3) Executed her own judgment, which is an extraordinary coincidence. The breaking through (sudden manifestation) by the King-Who-Judges is essential in our concept of the End Times, speci. the Day of Judgment; it took place in TEARS & in our world identically (Daniel & Revelation may have overstressed the calamatous aspects for cautionary purposes). In each case, one man is to be destroyed, and then the apparatus of the state withers (see epilog in TEARS). But the main indication is that what most fundamentally takes place in each is the introduction, into the world, of the power of Christian love,b brought by God; and this is what ameliorates conditions, causing the state apparatus to wither, this, despite she overt negative judging; it is negative judging to remove one man in order to usher in this power of love brought by God from His realm to Earth. This is the essential basis of Christianity. In -7- TEARS this is expressed in the scene at the all-night gas station with the black man; in this world the only moment of that sort I saw was in Senator Weicker's speech about "enemies are to be loved." But that did take place right after the intervention. It was the initial turn of direction. All this makes the most sense if it is assumed that Nixon's evil transcended the ordinary, that he, like Hitler, was diabolic: the kingpin of evil. Joel pointed out last night that the U.S. is the pivot point of the world in terms of freedom; if the citadel (Washington DC) falls, the rest of the world will fall automatically, in terms of freedom. As he said, "Will Iceland intervene for us?" This strengthens my case regarding the . intervention, for self-evident reasons; Nixon, at the heart of the citaael, was at least functionally diabolic, if not intentionally so. (Joal, by the way, declared the Xerox letter pro¬ bably a US forgery, when I told him about the two letters; he is probably right; the assistance to me then makes more sense if this is the case. And it fits my two or so dreams later on.) So I say that TEARS, which was written in 1970, parallels exactly the events of 1974: in depicting the slave state, the reduc¬ tion to total despair followed by abrupt intervention and judgment, the (implied) removal of one man and finally the withering away of the state after the manifestation of love. It is as if the reign of power is followed by the reign of love, the latter entering the world from Heaven, and requiring for its manifestation the removal of one evil man — which is to say Satan at the heart of the citadel. -1- But subjectively speaking, the most astonishing events, in contrast to the great historic intervention plus the material in TEARS, were the elaborate changes made in me, end-time changes I am certain, the shaping me up to make me acceptable — for the day which in August did come (the pale white light). If there had been no historic changes or perceptions of them; if there had been no TEARS, what was left was still overwhelmingly miraculous and complicated and unprecedented...that is probably the
